subtopic: Learning to code from the internet
subtype: Approach: debugging by reading the error and isolating the cause [Thinking]
passage:
“It crashed again.” Reena leaned in close. “Devika, don't tell me. Let me read it.”
“Go on.”
“IndexError, list index out of range, line fourteen.” Reena frowned. “Line fourteen. Not line one, so the whole program isn't wrong.”
“Where's the list?”
“Line nine. Five items.” Reena counted under the breath. “And the loop goes up to six. Off by one?”
“Maybe. How could you check?”
“Comment out the bottom half first. If it runs, the trouble is down there.” Reena typed hash marks. The program ran. “Okay, bottom half.” Reena changed the six to a five and ran it. “One change. Works.”
Devika smiled. “Only one?”
“One at a time, or I'll never know which fixed it.”

qa.q: Which line did the error message point to?
What might Reena be feeling when asking Devika not to tell the answer?
qa.a: Determined and a little proud: Reena wants to work it out alone 🙂.

qa.q: What could Reena do if the error came back after the fix, and why?
qa.a: Print the values inside the loop and change one thing at a time, since checking after every change shows which change matters.

qa.q: How does Reena's approach look to Devika?
qa.a: Devika, who only asks questions, sees Reena reasoning step by step, and may feel it is better to let Reena find the fix than to hand it over.

grounding: A teen faced with a crash reads the error, isolates the cause by commenting out half the code and fixes one thing at a time.
